source.title: Visualizing and Understanding Generative Adversarial Networks (Extended Abstract)
source.authors: David Bau; Jun-Yan Zhu; Hendrik Strobelt; Bo-Lei Zhou; J. Tenenbaum; W. Freeman; A. Torralba

page_placements.theme: What units match, and how interpretable they are, varies with layer depth

record.file_problem: The provided text is a complete extended abstract, not the full GAN Dissection paper; it identifies itself as an abstract of an invited talk about that work.
record.tranche_reason: It measures interpretable units in GANs and compares architecture variations, bearing conceptually on V4's claim that architecture choices affect the number of interpretable units. It does not use the original language-model audit method.
record.gate_note: The study reports architecture-variant comparisons and layerwise observations about units matching semantic classes. It does not test the Qwen neuron-pole percentages, language-model scale or MoE claims, Inception cat-and-car example, attribution graphs, held-out explanation prediction, or automated explanation scores. It also reports GAN object insertions and ablations, but those outcomes do not directly measure any listed version; the artifact-ablation FID comparison is recorded under none. The human-preference table is flattened and its comparison layout is unclear, so no preference row is extracted.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (Progressive GAN generators), it compares counts of interpretable units across architecture variants. This bears on V4's claim that architecture choices raise the share of interpretable units. It does not test tools, language models or the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that many GAN units correspond to semantic objects or parts and causally affect synthesis. They add that architecture improvements raise unit interpretability alongside model quality, and that cross-layer suppression remains unexplained.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses thresholded unit featuremaps matched to supervised semantic segmentation, plus GAN activation interventions; it is not a language-model neuron-pole audit or held-out explanation test.
record.method_sensitivity: Unit semantics vary by layer. The reported counts of semantic matches also vary with minibatch-statistics awareness and pixelwise normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating 20 human-chosen artifact units lowers FID from 52.87 to 32.11; ablating 20 random units gives 52.27.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual GAN units identified by inspection can be causally edited to remove artifacts.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantic object and part units concentrate in layers 4–7. Layer1 has almost none, and layers 10 and beyond mainly match materials and shapes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GAN generators, the kind of concept a unit matches varies by layer depth.

record.peer_reviewed: arXiv.org; the text says the underlying work was originally presented at ICLR 2019
record.problems: The architecture comparisons give relative increases without underlying counts or uncertainty estimates. Layerwise interpretability is qualitative in the prose, and the text does not quantify the overall share of interpretable units.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results left out. The human-preference entries in Table 1 were not extracted because the flattened table does not make the comparison layout clear.

untested.parts: Effect of better tools, of regularization, and of modern versus older architectures on the share; the InceptionV1-sized estimates (about 5% to about 99%); vision classifiers; and whether late-layer messiness is caused by architecture.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.
Explanations from activating examples versus held-out prediction.

missing.what: Absolute interpretable-unit counts per architecture variant (about 167, 189 and 226 of 512, as parsed) and SWD values (7.60, 6.48, 4.01).
Per-layer counts of object, part and material units (for example layer1: 0/2/0 of 512).
Human preference scores: 79.0% for artifact-ablated images and 50.8% for random ablation.

record.verdict_notes: The text is an extended abstract of GAN Dissection. The only variable that bears on V4 is a pair of 2018 GAN training innovations, so this is weak, setting-specific support. The earlier limits_scope label based on layer rows was removed because those rows do not test V4.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares and one-job, two-job, and not-understood categories.
Language models, dense versus MoE models, and scaling to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, and recursive generalization versus superposition.

The study tests architecture-variant and layerwise differences in GAN unit interpretability, but not weak tools, the claimed Inception-sized vision-model estimates, or whether tools and modern architectures raise the overall share to about 99%.
Attribution graphs, reconstruction error, and whether graphs built from a large model's neurons explain its behaviour without a replacement model.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples fail to predict firing on separate examples.
Automated simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations on new text.
